confidence_notes: I made one RBA search and five price searches, which returned only aggregator and crowdsourced figures (Expatistan, Hikersbay, Almurakib, citycost). These disagree by up to about 70%, for example cappuccino $2.0 to $3.50, beer $3 to $6, and inexpensive meal $10 to $25. Some are in pesos and dated, and Argentine inflation and FX move quickly. Beer, coffee and meal anchors are bounded midpoints of those ranges, with the beer figure for a restaurant draft. The cocktail anchor rests on an Expatistan downtown-club figure (about ARS 14,900, only 2 data points) and my sense of restaurant pricing. No source gave a restaurant price per glass of wine, so I set it from the beer price relationship and bottle prices, roughly 1.2 to 1.3 times beer. The mid-range meal for two is the least certain food figure, because the sources range from $33 to $60. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge for a July (winter, non-peak) window. I did not search for or inspect any accommodation listings or booking pages, so they are the least verified.
comparable_city_reasoning: Ushuaia is Argentina's priciest tourist destination, with a remote location, a cruise and Antarctica gateway role, and Tierra del Fuego logistics costs. I priced it above Buenos Aires and Mendoza and close to El Calafate and Bariloche, using aggregator price points converted at recent ARS/USD levels.
